[FACT] User is interested in starting a small herb garden in their kitchen window.

[PREFERENCE] User prefers to start with basil and mint for their herb garden.

[ASSISTANT] Recommended beginner-friendly herbs for indoor gardening: basil, cilantro, parsley, chives, mint, and thyme.

[ASSISTANT] Suggested that if the kitchen window receives direct sunlight for at least 4-6 hours a day, user can grow herbs that require more light, like basil and mint.

[ASSISTANT] Advised user to choose a container with good drainage holes for their herb garden.

[ASSISTANT] Recommended using a well-draining potting mix specifically designed for indoor plants.

[ASSISTANT] Suggested using grow lights if the window doesn't receive direct sunlight.

[ASSISTANT] Provided instructions for planting and caring for herbs, including sowing seeds or planting seedlings, watering when the soil feels dry, maintaining temperatures between 65°F to 75°F (18°C to 24°C), fertilizing once a month, and pruning to encourage growth.

[ASSISTANT] Suggested keeping the herb garden small initially and monitoring humidity.

[ASSISTANT] Advised checking for pests regularly.

[PREFERENCE] User is interested in making Japanese-style dishes with their favorite Japanese short-grain rice.

[ASSISTANT] Suggested simple Japanese-style sauces: Sesame Ginger Sauce and Mentsuyu (Noodle Sauce).

[ASSISTANT] Recommended making Onigiri (triangular rice balls) and provided tips for shaping them perfectly.

[ASSISTANT] Suggested wrapping onigiri individually in plastic wrap or aluminum foil and storing them in an airtight container to keep them fresh.

[ASSISTANT] Advised refrigerating onigiri at a temperature of 40°F (4°C) or below.

[ASSISTANT] Provided tips for preventing onigiri from drying out, including using short-grain rice, cooling the rice to room temperature, and moistening hands while shaping.

[PREFERENCE] User plans to wrap onigiri individually in plastic wrap and store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for easy access as a quick lunch or snack.
